topic: The WeWork $47B Implosion and Corporate Governance Failure
verification_standard: YTF Master Production System v2.0 - Section 6

key_evidence: Dedication: 'We dedicate this to the energy of we - greater than any one of us but inside each of us.'
Financials 2016-2018: 2016 revenue $436M, net loss $429.7M; 2017 revenue $886M, net loss $890M; 2018 revenue $1.82B, net loss $1.93B.
Six months ended June 30, 2019: Revenue $1.54B, Net loss attributable to WeWork $904.7M.
Future undiscounted lease commitments: $47.2 billion owed to landlords, against committed member backlog of roughly $4.0 billion.
Community Adjusted EBITDA: Custom non-GAAP metric that eliminated building-level operating expenses (including lease/rent costs), depreciation, amortization, and stock-based compensation.
Voting Control: Class B and Class C common stock carried 20 votes per share, giving Adam Neumann total majority voting control.

Successor Committee: Disclosed that Rebekah Neumann (along with Bruce Dunlevie and Steven Langman) would pick successor CEO if Adam died or became permanently disabled within 10 years, bypassing board majority vote.

sources.document_type: Form S-1/A (Amendment No. 1 to Registration Statement)
key_evidence: Amendment following market backlash: Reduced Adam Neumann's high-vote shares from 20 votes per share to 10 votes per share.
Removed Rebekah Neumann from the CEO succession selection committee.
Disclosed that the $5.9M paid to WE Holdings LLC for the 'We' trademark had been returned/unwound, with the trademark assigned back to the company for zero consideration.

sources.case_name: In re WeWork Litigation / Adam Neumann v. SoftBank Group Corp.
key_evidence: Disclosed terms of SoftBank's abandoned $3 billion tender offer (October 2019 Master Transaction Agreement).

Terms of the February 2021 settlement: SoftBank agreed to pay $1.6 billion total tender; Adam Neumann cashed out roughly $480 million in stock, received a $50 million legal fee allowance, a $50 million non-compete payout, and a five-year extension on a $430 million SoftBank loan.

sources.institution: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey
sources.document_type: Voluntary Petition for Non-Individuals Filing for Bankruptcy (Chapter 11)
key_evidence: Listed estimated liabilities between $10 billion and $50 billion against estimated assets between $10 billion and $50 billion.
Disclosed ongoing annual rent burden of approximately $2.7 billion (nearly 80% of total revenue).

Pre-petition common equity wiped out; emergence plan approved in May 2024 eliminating $4 billion in debt and transferring ownership to senior lenders (Cupcake Acquisition LLC / Yardi Systems and creditors).

sources.headline: ‘This Is Not the Way Everybody Behaves’: How Adam Neumann’s Over-the-Top Style Built WeWork
key_evidence: Documented corporate culture: Tequila Don Julio 1942 toasts, mandatory summer camp festivals, barefoot office strolls.
Purchase of a Gulfstream G650 for $60 million by WeWork for executive and family travel.
Details on Adam Neumann selling and borrowing against WeWork stock to the tune of more than $700 million prior to the IPO.

sources.headline: SoftBank Reaches $9.5 Billion Deal to Take Over WeWork
key_evidence: SoftBank agreed to provide $5 billion in new debt, accelerate a $1.5 billion warrant commitment, and tender for up to $3 billion in shares.
WeWork was projected to run out of cash by mid-November 2019 without emergency funding.
Valuation cratered from $47 billion in January 2019 to less than $8 billion in the rescue recapitalization.

sources.headline: Inside The SoftBank-WeWork Deal: How Masayoshi Son's Crazy Bet Crushed SoftBank
key_evidence: Documented the December 2016 12-minute tour in New York City with Masayoshi Son.
Verified quote: 'In a fight, who wins—the smart guy or the crazy guy? ... Crazy guy. ... You are not crazy enough.'
Son instructed Neumann to make WeWork ten times bigger than originally planned.

sources.headline: WeWork had a $6 billion debt deal contingent on raising $3 billion in an IPO — and now that whole package is in jeopardy
key_evidence: Details of the JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs credit facility: $6B in total loans and letters of credit, expressly conditioned on WeWork raising at least $3 billion in its equity IPO.
When the IPO was pulled, the $6 billion line vanished instantly, triggering the acute cash crisis.

sources.institution: No Mercy / No Malice (Prof. Scott Galloway)
sources.headline: WeWTF
key_evidence: Calculated that WeWork was incinerating $219,000 every hour of every day for an entire year ($5.2M per day).

Compared valuation multiples: IWG (Regus) had 3,300 locations, 400,000 members, $3.4B revenue, and was profitable with a $4B market cap; WeWork had 425 locations, 527,000 members, $1.8B revenue, lost $1.9B, yet was seeking a $47B valuation.
